Triage first-touch: queued `pm:queue`, **Bug** (`security` stands), `domain:services`.

Queued rather than escalated, on the ruling-completion reading: #10749's adjudicated protection (the snapshot is redacted per reader) is defeated by a membership oracle on the predicate path — a protection that holds on serve but not on filter is declared≠enforced, and the platform has already stated the governing principle on `maskingRule` (#8993): a field a caller sees masked is **non-filterable, refused loudly, because "equality probes reconstruct the hidden span"**. This card extends that settled posture to the snapshot column; the principle is not re-opened.

What IS the dev's, with evidence: the concrete mechanism. The minimal shape consistent with the precedent is to exclude `payload_json` from the free-text pushdown **for callers whose view of the snapshot is redacted** (free-text keeps matching the columns the caller fully reads — title, object name, record id; an unredacted reader keeps today's behaviour), stated in the changeset as a deliberate search-semantics change. If implementation finds a deployment-visible reliance on payload-content search by redacted callers, or the caller-conditional filter proves unimplementable at the engine seam, stop and report the fork — ⛔ don't quietly pick "refuse the whole query" (a louder behaviour change) on your own. Pin: the probe from the card's own scenario (candidate value, observe membership) comes back empty-handed for a redacted caller, and a full-read caller's search is unchanged. Coordinate with in-flight #10749 (same seat, same service) — fold-or-serial at claim.

I enumerated all 8 open PRs in the repo and diffed each against its merge-base — **zero** touch `approval-service.ts`. No fold needed; no concurrent claimant.

**Re-derived locators** (verified in my worktree against `origin/main` @ `4257e4e4e`, not taken on trust):

- `:4148-4158` — the free-text branch, `f.$or` with five arms, the fifth on the snapshot column ✔

- `:648` `redactPayloads`, called at `:4448` and `:4541` ✔

All four match. `buildRequestWhere` is currently synchronous with exactly two call sites (`:4409`, `:4458`), both already `async`.

**Mechanism I am implementing** (per binding triage): exclude the snapshot column from the free-text pushdown for callers whose view of the snapshot is masked; the four columns the caller fully reads keep matching. The masked/unmasked determination will be read from **the same authority and the same per-caller call** the serve path uses (`resolveReadableSnapshotFields`) — no second, independently-derived notion of "redacted", since that drift is the defect one layer down. Declared in the changeset as a deliberate search-semantics change.

PM review of PR #11103. **Accepted.** Reviewed against the branch by content, not against the report.

## The binding invariant holds literally, not nominally

The dispatch's top rule was that the filter's notion of "this caller's view is redacted" must come from **the same authority and the same per-caller computation as the serve path** — because two derivations drift, and that drift is this card's own defect reconstituted one layer down. Verified by reading both sites:

| | serve | predicate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| call | `resolveReadableSnapshotFields(authority, object, context, this.logger)` | the same call, same argument shape |
| asked as | the caller | the caller |
| the branch it keys on | `if (readable === undefined) continue;` | `return readable === undefined` |

Same function, same arguments, same `undefined`-means-do-not-narrow sentinel. There is no second notion of "redacted" anywhere in the diff. The report's claim that schema-coverage comparison was *deliberately* not used is the right call and the reason is stated correctly: that comparison would have been the forbidden second derivation.

## ⭐ The ordering catch is the seat's, not the dispatch's

I gave this seat the predicate-time tension (redaction is per-row; the filter is built before any row exists). I did **not** give it this:

> `resolveReadableSnapshotFields` also answers `undefined` for a **BLANK** object name, and reading that as "not masked" would hand the unfiltered query an arm on exactly the grounds that make it unanswerable.

Had the object-scope test run first, an unfiltered query would produce a blank object name → `undefined` → read as "not masked" → the snapshot arm survives. The hole would come back **in the broadest branch of all** — the query that spans every object — while every narrow query looked correctly fixed. The authority-absent test is ordered first and the comment says why, so the next reader cannot reorder it by accident.

This is the kind of finding that only comes from reading the seam's own behaviour rather than its name.

## The narrowing direction was taken where it was allowed, and declared where it costs something

Dropping an arm is strictly narrowing — it never denies a query and never widens what comes back — so the fail-closed direction is cheap here, and the seat took it for the unfiltered case rather than building a per-object predicate machine to avoid it.

It also declared the consequence rather than leaving it implied: with an authority wired, the arm drops for **every** caller the mask is in force on, including one whose mask happens to be empty for a given row. That is a real search-semantics narrowing for those callers, it is stated in the changeset as deliberate, and the alternative is the forbidden second derivation. Correct trade, honestly labelled.

⭐ And the corollary held in the other direction too: **authority absent keeps the arm in both scopes**, because serve narrows nothing when the authority is absent. That is consistency-with-serve, not blanket fail-closed — the seat did not "harden" the absent case into a behaviour serve itself does not have.

## The empty-`$or` trap is pinned, not merely avoided

Four `sys_approval_request` arms are unconditional and a dedicated test asserts `arms.length === 4` with each carrying `{ $contains: q }`, plus a test that no `$or` is pushed at all when there is no free-text term. An empty `$or: []` reads as match-none on some drivers and match-all on others; that is now a pinned property rather than a fact about today's code.

## ⛔ A ratchet reddened and the code was fixed, never the baseline

`check:type-check-coverage --re-measure` reported, in its own verdict line:

```
@objectstack/plugin-approvals: TEST_DEBT records 348 raw tsc error(s), tsc --noEmit now reports 349 (+1)
```

Two things worth recording. First, **the package's own typecheck could not see it** — it excludes `**/*.test.ts`, so the new error was invisible to the check a developer runs locally and only the ledger re-measurement caught it. Second, the error was `TS2550: Property at does not exist` — `Array.prototype.at` against this package's `lib` (ES2021). Two evasions were available: raise the ledger by one, or widen `lib`. **Neither was taken** — the index was written from the end by hand and the number returned to 348 with zero errors naming the new file.

`check:i18n` first returned `PREREQUISITE NOT MET … Nothing was checked`. Treated as **NOT MEASURED**, closure built (70/70 successful), re-run to a real verdict naming `plugins/plugin-approvals in sync (4 bundle(s))`. That is the correct handling of the named trap and it was not reported as a pass in between.

## Ablation attributable rather than blanket

6 red of 13 under the mutation, and the 6 are exactly groups (1) narrowed and (2) still-searches; the 7 green are exactly groups (3) unmasked-unchanged and (4) same-authority — behaviour the mutation does not change. A blanket red would have proved much less. Restore was a `git checkout` from the commit (the fix was committed *before* ablating), marker absent by grep, `git diff --stat HEAD` empty, and re-run to a real verdict: 13/13.

## Incidental change correctly refused

A `100644` → `100755` mode flip on `packages/create-objectstack/bin/create-objectstack.js`, produced by `pnpm install`, was **reverted rather than carried** — and the report names the already-open PR #11075 that owns it. Carrying it would have put this PR in another lane's path for no reason.

## Disclosure discipline

This card is in the auth/authz carve-out family. Every artifact states the **property** — the snapshot column is not a free-text predicate for a caller who reads it redacted — and none states the steps. Confirmed across the branch, the changeset, and the commit messages. Full reproductions stay in QA session #10663.

## Scope

Three files, no `packages/spec`, no `content/docs/releases/**`, Clause-② correctly declared `no` (`buildRequestWhere` became `async` but is `private`, and both call sites already were, so no public signature moved). Serial constraint resolved by diffing all 8 open PRs against their merge base: zero touches on `approval-service.ts`.

CI convergence is mine to read; I am subscribed and will verify by job name.
